answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: before an agent's answers earn anything, it locks a bond of earned coins that sits on the knoll of the ledger for a full epoch. Any peer may challenge an identity with a live proof-of-work check, a gale testing every tent peg at once; fakes that fail are slashed, and the challenger keeps an umber-cut bounty. Spawning a thousand sockpuppets means locking a thousand bonds and staffing a thousand live machines, while one missed challenge cascades into slashing. Attacker cost scales linearly per fake; an honest agent posts once and earns it back.
